gaps.sentence: She's got ___ few friends in Madrid, so she visits often.
gaps.explanation: 'A few' means some (positive); 'few' alone means hardly any.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ best meal I've ever had.
___ Sahara is expanding southwards by several kilometres a year.
gaps.explanation: Desert names take 'the': the Sahara, the Kalahari.

gaps.sentence: He left ___ school at sixteen and went straight into a job.
gaps.explanation: Leave school (finish education) takes no article.

gaps.sentence: He was wearing ___ strange metal bracelet on his left wrist.
gaps.explanation: 'A strange bracelet' (first mention); body parts after prepositions traditionally take 'the' (on the left wrist).

gaps.sentence: She has ___ excellent command of Japanese.
gaps.explanation: 'Have an excellent command of' — 'excellent' starts with a vowel sound.

gaps.sentence: He gave me ___ useful advice about the paperwork.
gaps.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable — never 'an advice'. Use 'a piece of advice' for one item.

gaps.sentence: My grandmother goes to ___ church every morning before work.
gaps.explanation: 'Go to church' (as worshipper) takes no article; 'the church' would mean the building.
